notes:
PASS on the fake backend (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), no hardware was attached or run, and no hardware backend was invoked. The card's entry_symbols list is empty, so there was no entry symbol to verify; the three card model files exist at the pinned commit. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: none; the family-config decision and MujocoDriver helper match the upstream, which is a pure MJCF model collection with no Python package to install. The package serves the card's models[0], bi-franka_panda.xml: a fixed torso with a left arm (assets/chain0.xml) and a right arm (assets/chain1.xml), 18 one-DOF joints and 16 position actuators (seven left arm, seven right arm, two right fingers; the left finger joints have no actuator). The bridge derives action.ctrl per actuator from the model's ctrlrange, the step writes data.ctrl and runs mj_step, and reset restores the model defaults. The world state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed). Mode simulated, risk R0: the driver advances a MuJoCo model and has no hardware backend, so it cannot move a robot arm or produce a physical effect; the card's risk_floor is R0 and both cap.world classes are R0. The other two card models (franka_panda.xml and franka_panda_teleop.xml) are not served by this package; one package serves one model.

The fake backend is fake.py, a pure Python stand-in for the mujoco library. It parses the served scene and its <include> elements for 18 joints, 16 actuator ctrlranges and the 2 ms timestep from assets/assets.xml:12, and implements the part of the mujoco API the bridge calls (MjModel/MjData, mj_resetData, mj_forward, mj_step, and the integration-state snapshot functions). It is not MuJoCo: it loads no mesh or texture, resolves no contact, equality, tendon or actuator dynamics, and integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its control value. MuJoCo itself was not installed or importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine and the sim path (a backend not listed in backends, which imports the real mujoco module) was not run.

NOT COVERED: the MuJoCo engine and the real engine's trajectory; the other two card models; the STL mesh assets and rendering/cameras; the Franka_wrist_cam image and the joint sensors; contact, equality and actuator dynamics; the model's actual joint-limit clamping (the fake does not clamp, and several actuator ctrlranges are wider than the corresponding joint range, e.g. panda0_joint1); the left gripper's two unactuated finger joints; and any physical Franka hardware. The real MuJoCo load of the served scene was not run either; the scene has a stray '/' after the closing default element at bi-franka_panda.xml:18, which ElementTree treats as text and the fake ignores. A local probe of mhs.snapshot + mhs.restore on this MuJoCo driver is refused at restore with MHS.CONFLICT.STATE_HASH: the server hashes the live resource state while the MuJoCo bridge snapshots its integration state. This is outside the gate's CL3 checks (FID-016 is CL4) and is recorded here as an SDK limitation; the fidelity contract still declares snapshot_restore true because the MuJoCo bridge and this fake expose the snapshot functions.

Expected warnings, all left as the family requires: G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND (the fake is the package's stand-in for the mujoco library and is named as a class object, so there is no recorded native surface for G7 to compare), and G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived integer ticks, the simulator's action.ctrl elements and the reset seed. G4 had no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warnings; every Fact cites a README or MJCF line of the clone at b54d271388cf9b179d3fb6cff7a430040afca33f. No operator-required limit is declared and no site-limits.example.json is needed: the envelope is derived from the model's actuator ctrlranges. No catalogue_requests: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used.
